# snagentic repository instructions

Use the `snagentic_*` Copilot CLI tools instead of constructing ServiceNow HTTP
requests or invoking the Python CLI through an interpolated shell command.

## Instance mirror workflow (preferred)

Instances live in `instances/<name>/` with a remote-only mirror branch
`servicenow-remote/<name>`. Use the `snagentic_instance_*` tools:

1. `snagentic_instance_fetch`, then `snagentic_instance_integrate`. Resolve
   conflict markers in `instances/<name>/metadata/` and commit before planning.
2. Understand before changing. The mirror contains every metadata record, out of
   box included, with its code. Start with `snagentic_instance_table` for each table
   involved (fields, inheritance, and all behaviour with paths), then read the
   `record.yaml` and script files it points to, and follow calls with
   `snagentic_instance_search` / `snagentic_instance_refs`. Flow logic, form layouts
   and workflow activities are read-only in `_children/`. Check
   `snagentic_instance_activity` and `snagentic_instance_collisions` for work
   other people have in progress. The `servicenow-capability` prompt covers the
   full analyse-and-build flow.
3. Edit only `instances/<name>/metadata/`. A new record is a new directory with
   `record.yaml` (plus optional `<field>.<ext>` files) and no `sys_id`. Never
   edit `_meta.yaml`, `_children/`, `model/`, `update-sets/`, or the mirror branch.
4. Run `snagentic_instance_plan` and show the user the changes, collisions and
   best-practice `review` findings (rule IDs such as `SN-PERF-001`) and the `gate`.
   Fix `block` findings; never write `waivers.yaml` yourself, a human approves waivers.
   The `servicenow-architect` and `servicenow-reviewer` skills and agents, plus the
   `servicenow-*` scripting, client, security and integration skills, hold the standards.
   For significant changes, delegate the review to the `servicenow-reviewer` agent, which
   records its verdict with `snagentic_instance_review_record`.
5. Only after explicit approval, call `snagentic_instance_apply` with
   `instance`, `planId`, and `confirm: true`. Use `allowCollisions` only when
   the user accepted the collision. Apply is refused while the standards gate fails.
   Afterwards run `snagentic_instance_scan` (ServiceNow Instance Scan) and report its
   findings before promoting.
6. Prefer `snagentic_instance_ops_run` (CI/CD API) over UI recipes. Run
   `snagentic_instance_ui_run` with `dryRun: true` first; real runs need
   approval and `confirm: true`.
7. `snagentic_instance_promote` completes agent update sets on development.
   Never apply, run operations, or run UI recipes against test or production.

Documentation: keep reviewed capability, process, and guide sources under
`instances/<name>/documentation/`; `instances/<name>/docs/` is generated output.
Use `snagentic_instance_docs` to scaffold, build, check, or migrate legacy narrative
blocks. Link technical claims to mirrored evidence and require human review for purpose,
benefits, ownership, and user instructions. Never include property values, credentials,
personal data, or business records.

## Legacy engine workflow

1. Run `snagentic_validate` for the intended environment.
2. Use `snagentic_inventory` or `snagentic_pull` to inspect or refresh the
   allowlisted artifacts.
3. Edit only normalized files under `servicenow/`.
4. Review `snagentic_status` or `snagentic_diff`.
5. Generate and review `snagentic_push_plan`.
6. Use `snagentic_push` only with an explicit environment whose configured
   `kind` is `development`, only after explicit user confirmation, and only
   with `confirm: true`.

Never push to test or production. Promotion to those environments must use the
supported ServiceNow deployment process. Never expose credentials in prompts,
tool arguments, logs, repository files, diffs, or generated documentation.

## Repository boundaries

- `instances/<name>/instance.yaml` stores only non-secret settings and
  environment-variable names (`SNAGENTIC_<NAME>_USERNAME` etc.).
- `servicenow/` is generated by pull, then intentionally reviewed and edited as
  the version-controlled artifact workspace.
- `.snagentic/` contains local baselines, raw state, diagnostics, locks, and the
  search index, mirror work trees, UI evidence, and promotion manifests. It is
  local-only and must not be committed.
- `config/snagentic.yaml` is local configuration. Store only environment-variable
  names there; never store token, username, or password values.
- `config/snagentic.example.yaml` documents safe, non-secret configuration.
- Diagnostics are local-only and may be cited by path, but their contents must
  not be copied into source control without a separate redaction review.

Prefer `snagentic_query` for local indexed searches. Treat pull as a local
workspace replacement: preserve or commit intended edits before refreshing.

The extension runs the installed native `snagentic` executable when one is found
(`SNAGENTIC_EXECUTABLE`, the `snagentic copilot install` marker, or `PATH`), so neither
Docker nor host Python is required; credentials then come from the OS credential store
(`snagentic auth login`). Without a native install it falls back to
`docker compose run --rm -T cli`. An approved `SNAGENTIC_PYTHON` value enables the
explicit direct-Python override; it must be an absolute path or a simple
executable name and must never contain flags or shell syntax. See
`docs/native-install.md`.
